title:
Wave functions
are not real
dek: Ψ is a probability amplitude — a complex number whose square gives where you'll find the particle. Before measurement, the particle literally has no position.
quote: An electron in superposition doesn't have a hidden answer — it's not in state 1 OR state 2, it's in a hybrid state that doesn't exist in classical physics at all.
bullets: |Ψ|² is probability density, not physical wave amplitude
Superposition is not ignorance about a pre-existing state
Particle has no definite position until measurement forces one

title:
Collapse is
instantaneous
dek: When you press Measure, the smooth interference pattern snaps into a single eigenstate. All other components vanish at once — not gradually, not locally, everywhere.
quote: The system was in a superposition a fraction of a second ago, and now it's in exactly one eigenstate. The other components don't gradually fade — they vanish instantaneously across all of space.
bullets: Individual events are random; aggregate statistics are exact
Whether collapse is physical or apparent is still debated

title:
Particles
tunnel through
barriers
dek: A particle localized in one well can spontaneously appear in the other — not by going around the barrier, but by existing in both wells simultaneously during the tunneling event.
quote: A particle starting in one well oscillates between wells with frequency ΔE/ℏ. This is not a classical particle bouncing — it's quantum tunneling in the probability landscape.
bullets: Symmetric and antisymmetric states split by ΔE
Models: ammonia molecule inversion, superconducting qubits
Tunneling rate set by barrier height and width
